findings.title: consume_material accepts negative quantity and inflates inventory
findings.description: consume_material only rejects when current_stock < quantity. A negative quantity always passes that check (stock is never less than a negative number) and then executes current_stock -= quantity, which adds |quantity| to on-hand stock. No lower bound or absolute-value guard exists.
findings.impact: Attacker-controlled consume quantity creates phantom inventory. False stock hides stockouts, suppresses reorder alerts (get_low_stock_items), and can back false material-availability claims used for schedule progress or billing.
attack_path: 1. Seed or observe inventory with legitimate stock (e.g. 100 tons).
2. Call consume_material(material_code, quantity=-500) with attacker-controlled quantity.
3. Guard current_stock < quantity evaluates 100 < -500 → False, so the write proceeds.
4. Stock becomes 600; low-stock/reorder reports and downstream consumers trust inflated on-hand.
findings.remediation: Reject quantity <= 0. Require quantity <= current_stock using an explicit positive-quantity check before mutating stock. Log consumption with signed audit fields.

findings.title: create_order silently overwrites existing order_id including DELIVERED POs
findings.description: create_order writes self.orders[order_id] = order with no existence check. Reusing an order_id replaces a CONFIRMED/DELIVERED purchase order (including delivered_qty, total_cost, supplier, status) with a fresh DRAFT at attacker-chosen quantity/unit_cost. Prior Delivery records remain orphaned.
findings.impact: Financial/audit fraud: wipe a completed high-value PO, replace with a $1 DRAFT under an attacker supplier, erase delivered quantities from the order ledger while historical deliveries still reference the ID.
attack_path: 1. Legitimate flow creates PO-001, confirms it, and records full delivery (status=DELIVERED, total_cost large).
2. Attacker calls create_order(order_id='PO-001', quantity=1, unit_cost=1, supplier='Attacker').
3. Dict assignment overwrites the MaterialOrder object with no conflict error.
4. Order ledger now shows DRAFT/$1/Attacker; cost summaries and status reports no longer reflect the real delivered PO.
findings.remediation: Refuse create_order when order_id already exists (or allocate server-side IDs). Separately, never allow mutation of terminal statuses (DELIVERED/CANCELLED) without an audited amendment workflow.

findings.title: issue_po skips RFQ/quote gates and accepts unbounded/negative re-issuance
findings.description: issue_po sets status=PO_ISSUED from any prior state (including REQUISITIONED), accepts any float amount (including negative), and can be called again to overwrite vendor/po_number/po_amount. get_summary() totals po_amount directly into total_po_value.
findings.impact: Procurement commitment fraud: fabricate or inflate PO commitments without quotes, or re-issue a legitimate PO to a negative/attacker amount that zeros or reverses reported PO value used for budget and payables.
attack_path: 1. Item exists in REQUISITIONED (no RFQ/QUOTED).
2. Call issue_po(..., amount=9999999) → status jumps to PO_ISSUED; summary total_po_value inflates.
3. Optionally call issue_po again with amount=-450000 and attacker vendor.
4. total_po_value becomes negative / retargeted; downstream commitment reports are falsified.
findings.remediation: Allow issue_po only from QUOTED (or equivalent). Require amount > 0 and optionally amount within quote tolerance. Disallow re-issue without cancel/amend; keep immutable PO history.

findings.title: QUALIFIED ignores EMR and documents_received safety gates
findings.description: _evaluate_qualification stamps QUALIFIED when per-criterion mins and raw total_score >= 60 pass. It never consults emr_rate (Experience Modification Rate) collected at application time, never requires documents_received (insurance/bonding evidence), and never applies criteria.weight. A contractor with catastrophic EMR and empty document list still becomes QUALIFIED.
findings.impact: Safety/procurement bypass: dangerous subcontractors enter the qualified register and get_qualified() results used for award decisions, without EMR or insurance/bonding proof.
attack_path: 1. add_application(..., emr_rate=5.0) with documents_received left empty.
2. score_application with values that meet each min_score and sum to >= 60.
3. _evaluate_qualification sets status=QUALIFIED without EMR or document checks.
4. get_qualified(trade) returns the unsafe contractor for award/shortlist use.
findings.remediation: Hard-fail QUALIFIED when emr_rate exceeds a configured threshold or documents_received lacks required artifacts (insurance, bonding). Apply weights; clamp scores to [0, max_score].

findings.title: resolve_clash forges RESOLVED on CRITICAL hard clashes with only a free-text note
findings.description: resolve_clash sets status=RESOLVED and resolved_at for any clash_id with no severity gate, no prior ACTIVE/assignment requirement, no evidence attachment, and no APPROVED transition. A CRITICAL hard MEP-vs-structure clash in NEW can be cleared with notes='looks fine'.
findings.impact: Coordination/safety underreporting: critical geometric conflicts disappear from open-clash summaries, enabling construction sequencing decisions on a falsely clean clash report.
attack_path: 1. run_clash_detection produces CRITICAL HARD clashes (status=NEW).
2. Attacker calls resolve_clash(clash_id, 'looks fine') with no design change.
3. Clash status becomes RESOLVED; get_summary by_status no longer counts it as open.
4. Exported clash report shows critical conflicts cleared without remediation evidence.
findings.remediation: Require ACTIVE assignment, remediation evidence/model revision reference, and a separate APPROVED step by a coordinator role before CRITICAL/HARD clashes leave the open set. Disallow NEW→RESOLVED.
